searchText: Transactions pay the same base fee. They don't have to pay the same inclusion fee. So... are the wallets going to have 2 entries for people to make for their transactions?? One for overall cost of the transaction and one for the inclusion fee? Advanced wallets might. My expectation is that the simplest wallets (like CoinBase wallet) will set inclusion fee to something reasonable for you and set fee max to 2-3x what is necessary for next block inclusion and just inform the user of a fee range. Medium advanced wallets will let you set fee cap but will set inclusion fee for you. Highly advanced wallets will let you set both. For most users, the simple solution will work great! OK, so for those trying to do arbitrage trades and be placed at a specific place in the block, then those will be using the advanced wallets, right? Those people almost all use custom scripts, not a UI wallet. Got it. Thanks. correct me if i am wrong on this <@!301186049323958275> but another core benefit for this introduction of pricing "certainty" (almost) is not only to help aid the UX for L1 users but also provide a path for rollups to publish to L1 on a routine basis without needing to be in a bidding war (or have a human push the button on what pricing is needed). 1559 should lay the groundwork for L2s to publish reliably. You still need the bidding war, but L2s now can programmatically know how much is a "fair price to pay". So an L2 can use whatever scheme it wants to pay people to publish to L1 and it can know how much is "reasonable". gotcha.. thx Without it, you need to develop much more complex schemes like escalating gas prices until someone does it or something, which takes time.
